summary.headline: Chembond Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record Rs 101.4 crore, but management flagged a ~3% margin hit from war-driven input cost inflation.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 326.15 crore (up 12%), EBITDA of Rs 51 crore (up 7%) and PBT of Rs 45 crore (up 7%), with H2 revenue of Rs 188 crore, up 35% over H1. Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 101.4 crore and EBITDA of Rs 15.7 crore were the highest of the last nine quarters. Management said margins are under pressure from metal-linked raw material costs that rose after the war declaration, with force majeure invoked and public-sector customers resisting price changes. The call was held after the demerger, which moved the water and construction businesses into the new listed entity.

financial_highlights.change: Highest of last nine quarters; management said above Q4 FY25 and Q4 FY24

financial_highlights.value: Rs 46.3 crore (presentation also cites Rs 51 crore), 14% of sales
financial_highlights.change: Rs 51 crore is +7% YoY per management

segments.name: Water technologies
segments.commentary: About 87% of FY26 revenue and the fastest-growing unit; H2 revenue Rs 162 crore, up 36% over H1, with volume of 4,813 MT vs 3,205 MT... (H1 volume stated as 9,905 MT in transcript, which conflicts with H2 4,813 MT; not reconciled on call). Record single-month revenue of about Rs 32 crore in March.

segments.name: Construction chemicals
segments.commentary: About 7% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 13 crore vs H1 Rs 11 crore (+18-20%), H2 volume 2,590 MT (+30%). Management claimed PBT margin of about 20%; DSO about 88 days at 31 March 2026.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: About 6% of revenue; H2 revenue Rs 12.5 crore vs H1 Rs 9 crore (+40%), H2 volume 1,049 MT vs 594 MT in H1; DSO about 80 days.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene (JV with Calvatis)
segments.commentary: About 1% of revenue; H2 growth of 15%. Management described it as subpar for seven years, with early traction from integration into water channel.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 volume growth expected at about 15-20% in construction chemicals and about 10% in water chemicals.
Management said next four quarters at Rs 100 crore-plus are possible, subject to Q1 seasonality, and sequential quarters should improve on the prior year.
Around 3% margin impact seen in the immediate month from input cost inflation; a couple of quarters expected to pass costs through, with new contracts bid at higher prices.
Rs 1,000 crore revenue within four years described as an aspiration, not a commitment.
Water business entering FY27 with a strong chemicals and equipment order book; chemical contracts run to around mid-year, and FY27 budget already reflects the volume trend.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of about Rs 20-21 crore, mainly PPE transferred on the demerger and office renovation (management).
About Rs 65 crore of cash on books; management said some would go to network growth and geographic expansion, with no new plant planned.
Construction chemicals: de-bottlenecking of production lines; repair mortars outsourced to contract manufacturers.
Limited surplus water chemical inventory was rationed across customers during the force majeure period; volumes were kept below potential.
demand_pricing: Growth was mainly volume-driven, with new customer acquisition as the main driver; price growth contributed very little in FY26.
Construction chemicals realisation fell to about Rs 51,274/MT in H2 from about Rs 55,584/MT in H1, which management attributed to product mix (admixtures vs sealants).
Distribution realisation fell to about Rs 1.19 lakh/MT in H2 from about Rs 1.51 lakh/MT in H1, attributed to product mix.

Water business: about 70% private sector and 28-30% public sector (PSUs such as IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, NTPC, NPCIL). Private customers granted temporary price increases of 5-12% for about three months; public-sector customers refused to amend terms.
Input costs: metal-linked raw materials (zinc, molybdenum) rose from late February/March; management said 15 A-group items are up more than 120%.
Competitors named: Ecolab, Nalco, Solenis, Suez/Veolia, Ion Exchange, Thermax; Vasu Chemicals now owned by Dorf Ketal.
Largest customer under 5-6% of revenue; Nigeria export business exited after the customer refused LC terms.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Rs 100 crore-plus quarterly run-rate continue for the next four quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes is possible, with Q1 seasonally slower than Q4, but quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year comparisons should improve.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin pressure from input costs, and can margins return to last year's levels?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3% margin impact in the immediate month; cost pass-through takes a couple of quarters, and new contracts are being priced at higher baselines. Chemical prices have softened only slightly.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Fair-value adjustment on investments: net gain was lower than in the prior quarter and the loss on fair value of investments was higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why are construction and distribution realisations lower in H2 than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Product mix; admixtures lower realisation, sealants higher. Distribution is purely trading, so mix depends on customer demand.

qa_highlights.question: Can water business margins reach construction-level PBT of about 20%, and why are they lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peer margins are at par, within about 0.5 percentage points; employee cost is about 18% of revenue in water versus 14% in other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: What is the public/private split in water and how is force majeure being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Public sector is about 28-30% and private about 70%. Private customers accepted temporary increases; public-sector customers refused, and the company is preparing contingency actions if disruption extends beyond another month.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation in metal-linked raw materials; about 3% immediate margin impact and pass-through lag of a couple of quarters.
Public-sector water customers (28-30% of water revenue) refusing price amendments; force majeure invoked and contingency plans in place if disruption extends beyond about one month.
Working capital: DSO of about 88 days in construction and about 80 days in distribution.
Construction and distribution realisation decline from product mix; water realisation not disclosed on the call.
FY26 capex of about Rs 20-21 crore was largely demerger-related; further capex and cash deployment plans still unclear.
Data inconsistency: H2 water volume of 4,813 MT compared with 9,905 MT in H1 needs reconciliation; FY26 EBITDA quoted as both Rs 46.3 crore and Rs 51 crore.
summary.management_tone: Confident on revenue momentum and the order book, but cautious on margins; management repeatedly said near-term profitability is a challenge tied to the war-driven cost spike. Evasive on budgets and on the public-sector price question.
key_quotes: Unfortunately, this story has changed post this war, having started this financial year.
So it's a synergy with our water business that we are now exploiting more efficiently.
So the track remains positive and on the positive growth for all quarters.
Yes, it's possible, but some seasonality comes into this business.

growth.why: Management guides Rs 100 cr+ quarterly revenue possible over next four quarters, Q1 FY27 volume growth of 15-20% in construction chemicals and ~10% in water chemicals, backed by a strong water order book and volume-led new customer acquisition, but no new capacity is planned and a ~3% margin hit from input costs is flagged.
